solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starving artist's love consumed by fabulous woman

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed up and ends up inside it

parts.note: Venus, goddess of love, a woman of fable
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A painter goes hungry, his romance having eaten him up over a legendary beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The S after artist is just a possessive, not a letter to use; Venus is the goddess of fable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ravenous is extremely hungry, so the adjective works as a direct synonym for being famished.

clue.text: Addict eats large tart

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast, an addict of something
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on food scoffs a big pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, which is a kind of tart.

clue.text: Whips swab on board ship

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to swab is to wipe clean

explanation.surface: A sailor is punished with the lash for mopping the deck of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Whips is the slang verb for stealing, not the lash the nautical surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech to swipe something is to steal it, the same slang sense as whipping it.

clue.text: Power of Atlas's heart always on decline

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the five-letter name
ever means always, as in ever hopeful
to age is to grow old and decline

explanation.surface: The titan holding up the sky has a strong core but is forever weakening.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts EVER above AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is the power or influence gained from a position, as with a lever giving mechanical advantage.

clue.text: Dodgy hip, so rests getting replacement part?

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters are not to be trusted in the order given

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A patient with a bad hip rests up while waiting for a new joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a playful description, apt because a hip replacement is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial body part fitted to substitute for a missing or damaged one, such as a hip joint.

clue.text: Return of Queen left for pop

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A Queen comes back, having left the throne for the pop charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like the definition but is the reversal signal; the answer is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp bang of a gun firing, a sudden noise just like a pop.

clue.text: Sacred Hearts authorised

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
authorised means permitted, allowed

explanation.surface: Something about sacred hearts receiving official approval, as in religious devotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or consecrated, so it is a direct synonym of sacred.

clue.text: After party drop Ecstasy in prescribed amount

indicators.note: after places what follows behind the word for party in the sequence

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
to sag is to droop or drop
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: After a party someone takes a pill, but only in the measured quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests taking a pill, but it means sag.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the quantity of a medicine a doctor directs a patient to take at one time.

clue.text: Some learn education's merited

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters are taken

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Some people who learn have earned their schooling on merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To have earned something is to have deserved it through effort, the same as having merited it.

clue.text: Study accommodating a faculty head

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one word houses the other

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university study has room for the person running the department.
explanation.definitionFit: In a university the dean is the senior academic in charge of a faculty.

clue.text: Title and group's sound endlessly reviewed

parts.note: a posse is a group, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: viewed again from the other end, so read backwards
without its end, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a noise is a sound

explanation.surface: A band's title and their sound are endlessly reviewed by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: NOISE loses its last E to give NOIS, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, title means the right of ownership, and possession is having ownership of something.

clue.text: Beats English in defeats

indicators.note: in places one item within the other

parts.note: routs are heavy defeats
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: The English team is beaten in a string of heavy losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beats' looks like a verb meaning defeats, but it is the noun: a police officer's regular round.
explanation.definitionFit: A beat is the regular round a police officer patrols, so beats are habitual paths or routes.

clue.text: Teeming rain let loose under storm centre?

indicators.note: something let loose is set free from its order
in a down clue, under puts this part below the next
the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the middle three letters of the five
seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Rain unleashed beneath the eye of a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teeming' looks like part of the weather scene, but it is the definition, as in teeming with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrential rain falls in torrents, so torrential describes a downpour that is teeming.

clue.text: Lead or backing say covering Eminem's music smash

indicators.note: a cover goes around what it covers, so it wraps the rest
backing means going in reverse, so read the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what say means here
Eminem is a famous rapper
a smash is a hit record

explanation.surface: A dramatic lead or support covering one of Eminem's smash hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'; Eminem is an American rapper.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'lead' of a pencil is actually graphite, a soft form of carbon that writes.

clue.text: Beaten and stumped, confining runs

indicators.note: to confine is to shut something inside

parts.note: stuck means baffled, stumped
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman beaten and stumped, having scored few runs, in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words stumped and runs mislead: stumped means baffled. In cricket a batsman is stumped when the keeper breaks the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past participle of strike, so something struck has been hit or beaten.

clue.text: Drunk crashed a party game

indicators.note: drunk means staggering about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tipsy guest crashed a party game.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a party game in which players mime words or titles for others to guess.

clue.text: Puzzle tester's ends should include enjoyment

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so these letters go inside
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word tester
ease is comfort and pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone testing a puzzle insists the solving should be fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser, short for brainteaser, is a tricky question or puzzle to solve.

clue.text: Stiff, almost awake, embracing Frankenstein's helper

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside your arms
almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to rouse is to wake someone
Igor is the hunchbacked assistant in Frankenstein films

explanation.surface: A stiff body, barely awake, is held by the doctor's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Igor is the hunchbacked assistant of film versions of Frankenstein, not of Mary Shelley's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigorous means strict and inflexible, which is one sense of stiff, as in stiff regulations.

clue.text: Go back on promise arising in naive generosity

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means reading upwards, from the bottom
in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a pledge that arose from naive generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to fail to keep a promise or agreement, so it means to go back on one.

clue.text: Over in toilet are lots holding stomach?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so it is read backwards
the run of words holds the answer within

parts.note: the letters from the end of the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: The toilets are full of things held in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it, the idiom for enduring something unpleasant.

clue.text: Gloomy surrounded by very big smells

indicators.note: something surrounded is enclosed on every side

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size
dour means sullen and gloomy

explanation.surface: A gloomy figure is surrounded by large, smelly odours.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are scents, especially unpleasant ones, so the noun matches smells.

clue.text: Leave Scotland's leader in government

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the word

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule or government

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so take the first letter

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: The Scottish First Minister is told to leave office.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to quit a job or position, so it means to leave.

clue.text: Swam seeing fish in so-called foreign sea

indicators.note: in puts the fish inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Red Sea lies abroad and is called Red
an eel is a long fish

explanation.surface: A swimmer spots a fish in a distant sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Swam is not swimming, but the sense of a head that swam with dizziness.
explanation.definitionFit: When your head swims you feel dizzy, and to reel is to feel giddy in that same way.

clue.text: Criminal with bird in empty time break

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: in places the bird inside
an empty word has its inside removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters
a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: A criminal doing time inside a prison seeks a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' and 'time' are both slang for prison, and the surface uses them that way, but here bird is a raven.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a rule is to violate or breach it, so it means to break it.

clue.text: Old man about to get trim

parts.note: pa is father, an old man
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Dad is about to have his hair cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to cut away the outer edge of something, which is to trim it.

clue.text: Prudish, quietly covering skirt

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means placed above

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
a skirt is a border or edge, a rim

explanation.surface: A prudish person quietly covers up with a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' looks like clothing but here means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prim is stiffly formal and proper, easily shocked by rudeness, much the same as prudish.

clue.text: Concealed curve — advanced, taking two directions

parts.note: an arc is a curve
A is the abbreviation for advanced
N and E are north and east

explanation.surface: A hidden bend, advanced by taking two routes at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means mysterious and understood by few, so it describes knowledge kept secret or hidden.

clue.text: Retired with time sure to be wasted

indicators.note: being wasted means wrecked, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A retiree is certain their free time will be wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes someone retired from a post but keeping their title as an honour, such as a professor.
